rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Quality and Inner Melody in Poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong poem exhibits a peculiar musical quality or melody that inthralls the reader—an inner ear sense of melody not reducible to mechanical metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Melody should feel natural and perfect (compared to a Greek column); avoid artificial, demonstrable meter that lacks inner musicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigorous, Minute Analysis as a Literary Faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: One prime quality of literary genius is vigorous yet minute analysis: the ability to conceive truly, maintain a proper relation of parts, and draw a correct outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis facilitates purposeful construction: the author anticipates the desired effect and arranges subordinate parts to serve a common center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecundity of Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementing analysis, a high-quality writer shows a wonderful fecundity of imagination that groups, fills up, and colors the conceived outline with rich detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imaginative fecundity supplies the material that analysis shapes; both faculties together produce strong prose and poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposeful Construction and Unity of Parts
rubrics_metrics.description: All subordinate parts of a work should tend strictly to a common center; construction and form are essential merits of high art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the work so each element supports the intended emotional or intellectual effect—construction is judged as highly as material or subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Mystery and Minute Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective tales of the weird balance impalpable shadows of mystery with minuteness of detail (not leaving even a pin or button unnoticed) to throw reality into unreal fancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise detail to anchor imaginative or uncanny elements; mystery should be controlled and coherent, not merely vague or mystical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled (Mathematical) Mystery, Not Mysticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Mystery should be managed analytically—'mathematical' to the author's mind—rather than being vague mysticism that colors all thought without clear structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should understand their elements (the 'chemical properties of colors') and use mysterious elements as deliberate parts of design, not as unexplained atmosphere alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused Psychological Analysis (Monomania)
rubrics_metrics.description: Powerful fiction often dissects a monomania or single obsession in depth, tracing its subtle ramifications and presenting a concentrated psychological study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on a single dominant trait or obsession when exploring interior states; deep focus can yield strong horror or psychological realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished Style and Classical Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A high level of finish, grace, and classical form in prose and poetry is a mark of excellence—style should be highly finished and consistent with design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stylistic polish and formal control; a singular well-crafted tale can be sufficient to establish an author's genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine Horror/Terror With Other Qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: The great masters combine dread and horror with other qualities (household charm, beauty, or moral elements) rather than relying on dread alone to subjugate reader imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pure, unrelieved horror; mix terror with other human or aesthetic qualities to create fuller artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic Precision in Criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism should exhibit unerring analysis of diction, meter and plot, with scientific precision and coherent logic, even if it lacks warmth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytic tools to evaluate works; precise, logical critique is more valuable than vague generalities or partisan invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and Genuine Genius vs. Mere Talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine genius produces work with an irresistible magnetism and originality that mere talent cannot achieve; originality and 'innate experience' are distinguishers of highest merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek evidence of novel conception, strong individual voice, and the ability to move readers beyond technical competence.
